summary: Aggregate counts include 48 I.1 Preterit, 16 I.3 Infectum and 13 I.3 Preterit, plus sparse II/III material. Detailed occurrence decisions cover 74 supplied records only.

Removal alternates between transitive šləḥle and active-shaped intransitive šaləḥ/šaliḥi. Intransitive Infectum šoləḥ with flesh should not be relabelled Detransitive merely because it lacks an external agent.

mәšloḥo has a feminine husk subject at Lahdo The mill/3 and a separation mәnne at /2; these support a new Detransitive I Infectum box, while III mašləḥile removes clothing from people. II robbery and III robbery overlap semantically but retain their different forms.
The new oven-content frame at JL 9.10/13 changes the affected object; contrast direct detached bread at 73/259. The printed d- must be retained pending native confirmation.
Part. Pass. šliḥo in the patriarch’s threat denotes removal from clerical rank; it is not a description of undressing. Ordinary unsheathed swords remain the existing Detransitive sense 1.

Inherited branch placement conflicts with I.2 wording and with reader assignments. A single targeted example move aligns JL 8.11/4 and JL 11.11/8 without rewriting the inherited gloss. Hair-plucking remains I.1, following the inherited 75/157 parallel.
Repeated predicates, narrative restarts and repeated retellings (MAC ezo koviye/18–19) remain separate occurrence lines but are not multiplied as independent glossary examples.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
Round one already introduced III Infectum. The wedding token fills its thin cell; it is not a new box and no light-verb noun construction occurs.
New active Preterit-wa is independently attested both in military release and in literal removal of head coverings. The two senses remain separate despite sharing the same box.
I.1 Preterit already has five examples after round one; military and Arab clothing-removal tokens are not added on stale thin-cell grounds. I.1 Infectum is also full.

The exact military subject structure at 549 is less secure than the technical domain. The division may release people rather than itself set off; the machine English is quoted with its status explicit and is not used to decide that valency.
Confirm privative/container d- in gšəlḥina u=tanurayḏan du=laḥmo and the technical status of šliḥo in JTM 4.3/5.

Confirm Detransitive I mәšloḥo versus stem II mšalḥo in the milling description, and whether active-shaped flesh šoləḥ at JTM 5.2/100 has an omitted agent. The supplied syntax favours the analyses recorded here.
Check PrS 42/56: Turoyo removes a cap, German puts it on. No put-on meaning or invented correction is published.
Check anomalous košolanaḥne at 116/32 and mašlaḥhe at 95/65 against the edition; verify person/object contractions without silent normalization.
Confirm the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv filing of šloḥo at 67/178 and šlaḥto at 66/370. The nominal forms alone do not warrant a structural move.
Verify publication-number concordances prs 116/28 versus PrS 41/124 and prs 132/36 versus PrS 47/22 before altering those references.
At Jan 2.4/549 is i fərqa the releaser and šləḥḥe a transitive form, or is the division itself departing? Confirm the corresponding first-person gədšəlḥina.
Does the military sense denote formal discharge or simply permission to set off? The current gloss keeps both close readings.
At Jan 1.38/1671 do guests literally lose clothing, or does mašləḥile conventionally mean extracting money? No separate ritual idiom is accepted.
Is 116/30 intended as a parallel lexical reference rather than the source of this example?

summary: Does 44/92 belong only as a parallel use of šlaḥ?

The shared imperative is real, but this verse does not contain the quoted objects. The accompanying PrS 56/17 has not been verified here, so retain it and clarify whether 44/92 is merely supplementary.
